conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. You're here for severe abdominal pain. Can you tell me what’s been going on?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I’ve had this pain before. It started yesterday—mid-epigastric, really sharp. Nausea and vomiting too. Feels just like my pancreatitis flares.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that makes sense. You’ve had chronic pancreatitis for a while. Any fever, diarrhea, or blood in your stool?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No fever or diarrhea. Stools are formed, which is good—last time I was here, I had terrible diarrhea from C. diff.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good to know. We’ll test for C. diff again to be safe. We’re starting IV fluids and will manage your pain. We had trouble with your IV—needed a midline placed in your left arm.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, okay. That makes sense. It’s usually hard to get my veins. Is the midline going to stay in long?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just for this admission. It’ll help us give fluids and meds smoothly. We’re giving Dilaudid for pain and promethazine for nausea as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I’m glad it’s the usual protocol. I’m worried about my blood pressure too—it’s been high.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your BP was 159/116 on arrival. We held your hydrochlorothiazide because you’re a bit dehydrated—what we call hypovolemia. We’ll restart it once you’re more stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, okay. So that’s why I feel so lightheaded?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Fluids should help. We’re also watching your labs—lipase was only 36, which isn’t high, but given your history, we still think this is a pancreatitis flare.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s surprising. I thought lipase always went up during a flare.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not always, especially with chronic pancreatitis. Your symptoms and history are more telling. We’ll keep you NPO for now and slowly advance your diet.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. Can I try ice chips soon?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we can start those now. We’ll see how you do and try clear liquids tomorrow if nausea improves.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your C. diff test came back negative, so we’re not concerned about infection. That’s great news.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, that’s a relief. I was worried it came back.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We also reviewed your urine toxicology. It showed opiates and barbiturates. The opiate is likely from the hydromorphone you got in the ER, but the barbiturate is probably from Fioricet for migraines?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I take Fioricet when I have a bad headache. Is that a problem?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not a problem—we expected it. We just wanted to confirm and let your PCP know. Your serum tox screen also showed tricyclics, which matches your amitriptyline.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, that’s for my nerve pain and sleep. I take 75 mg at night.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. We’re continuing that. Now, your blood pressure is still high—151/99 this morning. Since we held HCTZ, we’re starting lisinopril to help control it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Should I keep taking both when I go home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll restart HCTZ and add lisinopril. We’ll monitor how you do. Any side effects like dizziness, let us know.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing well. You’ve been off IV pain meds since last night and are tolerating clear liquids. We’re advancing you to a soft diet today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great! I’m really hungry. Can I have some broth or applesauce?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, exactly. Start slow. We’ll also switch your pain meds to oral tramadol and keep promethazine for nausea as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’d prefer that. I don’t want to stay on IV narcotics.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing great with that. We’re proud of how you’ve stuck to your plan. No extra requests—very responsible.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your abdomen is less tender today, and bowel sounds are normal. You’ve gained a little weight—77.8 kg—so fluids are helping.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel better. The pain is mild now, just with eating a lot.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s expected. We’ll keep you on Creon with meals to help digestion. Your omeprazole is also helping with reflux, which can mimic pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I forgot to ask—should I keep taking Creon even when I feel fine?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, absolutely. It replaces enzymes your pancreas can’t make. Skipping it can trigger flares. Same with amitriptyline and quetiapine—keep those for mood and sleep.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. I’ve been stable mentally—no dark thoughts or anxiety.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s excellent. We’ll keep your lorazepam for anxiety and insomnia as needed. You’re on the right track.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re planning to discharge you tomorrow. You’re walking, eating well, and off IV meds. How are you feeling about that?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Really good. I’m ready to go home. Will I need the midline removed?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll remove it before you leave. You won’t need it anymore. We’re sending you home on all your usual meds, including tramadol for pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No new narcotics? I’m okay with that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No, we’re not prescribing any controlled substances. You’ve done so well without extra doses—we trust your plan.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I don’t want to depend on them.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. We’ll also give you instructions to follow up with your PCP and continue monitoring your blood pressure.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I need another scan or blood work soon?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your PCP may check labs, but no urgent imaging. Focus on diet—low fat, small meals—and avoid alcohol completely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I don’t drink, so that’s fine. And I’ll stick to my diet.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. We’re finalizing discharge. Your vitals are stable—BP 151/99, pain minimal. You’re cleared to go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Great! My wife is on her way. Thank you for taking care of me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re very welcome. Remember: take your meds, follow up, and call if pain worsens or you can’t keep food down.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. And thank you for explaining everything so clearly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Of course. Take care, and we hope not to see you back soon!

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Same here!

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Nurse will remove your midline and give you discharge papers. Your wife can bring the car around.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. I’m ready.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: One last thing—your contact, your wife, is listed. Call us or her if anything comes up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, she’s my main support. I’ll reach out if I need to.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Excellent. You’ve done really well this admission. Keep it up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll try. Thanks again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. See you in follow-up!

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Bye!
